newsitem.title: USA: Stocks depressed by HP sell-off, upbeat data.
newsitem.headline: Stocks depressed by HP sell-off, upbeat data.

text.p: Stocks fell sharply Friday as investors grew jittery after surprisingly strong economic news and disappointing earnings from Hewlett-Packard Co., one of the stocks in the Dow Jones industrial average.
At 1 p.m. EST, the 30-share Dow was off 62.64 points at 7,270.91, more than reversing Thursday's gains to a record 7,333.55. The Nasdaq composite shed 8.94 points to 1,344.64.
"The market is down because Hewlett-Packard led the market down on their earnings and there was a little profit-taking. Don't forget it's double witching day too," one trader said.
The "double witching" expiration of individual and index options often leads to volatility in the stock market.
Analysts said weakness in the bond market also depressed stocks after the release of upbeat U.S. April housing starts and University of Michigan consumer sentiment data.
The housing starts came in at a 1.47 million annual rate, compared to forecasts of 1.43 million. The preliminary index of consumer sentiment for May rose to 104.6 from 101.4 in the final April index.
The benchmark 30-year Treasury fell 15/32, raising the yield to 6.91 percent from 6.87 percent at Thursday's close. Prices and yields move in opposite directions.
Charles Pradilla, market analyst at Cowen & Co., said profit-taking, anticipation of the Federal Reserve's policy-making meeting on Tuesday and the Hewlett-Packard earnings combined to hurt stocks.
"You put all those together and we are down about one-half of a percent. It's not a big deal," Pradilla said.
Joel Calvo, president of PNC Brokerage Corp., said the market is absorbing mixed news as it awaits the meeting of Fed policy-makers who will decide their next move on interest rates.
"There continues to be a mixture of news whether it be earnings or economic news. And, of course, what is the Fed going to do?" Calvo said.
Meanwhile, the technology sector slumped, with several key Nasadaq stocks sharply off from Thursday.
Netscape Communications Corp. shares tumbled over 4-7/16 to 30-1/8 after the company issued a warning of slower earnings and revenue growth in a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission.
The Standard & Poor's index of 500 stocks fell 6.17 points to 835.71. The American Stock Exchange index added 1.99 points to 585.46.
